extracts.lead_summary: Last week the bid was flow. This week a company earned some of it. Procter & Gamble grew organic sales 4%, with 2.4 points of volume and every category and region up, and the stock rose 5.6% on Thursday to a 52-week closing high. XLP closed that day at $89.99, a new 52-week closing high and the top of the day's range, then gave back 1.9% on Friday to finish +0.73% at $88.26. Philip Morris gapped 6% lower on its print and closed nearly flat. The carry gap narrowed to -226bp as the 10Y slipped under 5%. I still do not buy the leaders at their targets, but I have to say plainly that the first quarter I asked for came in better than I expected.
